milestone.description: Phase 3 complete. All 14 implementation units (P3-01 through P3-14) plus the mid-phase P3-02 regression repair (D-0053) and P3-EXIT (evidence assembly, Production Readiness Report, Level 3 independent review across 2 rounds) are done. Round 1 found and this build fixed 1 real CRITICAL DEFECT (a billing webhook crash on the single most common real-world Stripe event) plus 4 non-blocking findings; round 2 independently re-verified the critical fix, found 0 new CRITICAL DEFECTs, and 3 new non-blocking findings in adjacent untested paths of the same defect classes -- all fixed proactively. Full validation at close: 678/678 unit+integration tests, 24/24 e2e, clean typecheck/lint/format, production build succeeds.

architecturalStandards.name: Practical product completeness (common-sense product reasoning)
architecturalStandards.summary: Pocket Studio must reason about the normal supporting behavior a requested capability implies (affordances, workflow continuity, state completeness, data lifecycle, validation, accessibility, permissions/consequences, product continuity, customer-perceived completeness) — not just literal requirement/component compliance. Every implied behavior is classified REQUIRED, CONVENTIONALLY_IMPLIED, RECOMMENDED, OPTIONAL, CONSEQUENTIAL_DECISION (never silently approved — surface via the Decision Ledger), UNSUPPORTED (represent truthfully), or UNRESOLVED (ask or record). See src/lib/generation/interaction-contracts.ts's module comment for the initial foundation.
architecturalStandards.firstVerticalProofTarget: DELIVERED (P2-EXIT practical-completeness repair, commit d912048, Level 3 review round 1 accepted after 2 real findings were fixed): the Example App Ideas picker (src/components/example-idea-picker.tsx) is a real Studio UI feature — selectable by mouse, keyboard, and touch (independently verified live in a browser via e2e/example-idea-picker.spec.ts, including a real hasTouch browser context), populates its connected textarea while remaining fully editable, behaves predictably under repeated selection, preserves the customer's exact attempted text through a recoverable minimum-length-validation failure, and lets the customer continue naturally into a real generation. Registered as a real, SUPPORTED_NOW platform Capability Registry entry (studio.example_app_ideas_picker) rather than per-project Truth Status, since it is a fixed Studio feature, not a per-customer capability.
architecturalStandards.status: Interaction Contract System pipeline substantially strengthened at P2-EXIT (commit d912048, Level 3-reviewed): interactionContracts is now a required, validated Blueprint field covering both screens and workflows (previously optional, silently skippable); the classification vocabulary covers 6 real values (required/conventionally_implied/recommended/optional/consequential_decision/unresolved) plus a real explicit/inferred basis axis and a real unsupportedStates capability-gap mechanism; the Build Planner consumes workflow contracts for real per-state tests; the renderer implements retry and disabled-while-pending for real (not just declared); the Quality Gate grew from 8 to 11 checks (unsupported-state detection, consequential/unresolved-disclosure re-verification, unwired-Button detection) and gained 5 real per-dimension Truth Status keys alongside the flat rollup; restore-validation now re-checks contract completeness. Known, disclosed, non-blocking gaps remain: no 'selectable list item' interaction state is modeled (list items render as static text, not clickable/keyboard-navigable — a real gap in the state vocabulary itself, not just its implementation); search/filter, pricing/plan-selection, and destructive-action-beyond-payment pattern families are not yet modeled as their own ProductPattern entries; mobile output (P2-15) has no equivalent Interaction Contract enforcement at all (its own disclosed scaffold-only limitation); the openDecisions disclosure-verification check matches on free-text substrings, fragile to future message-format drift though no live collision exists today.

P2-07: Demonstration product — closed the P2-06 placeholder-Form gap generically (Form Inputs now named after a bound data model's real fields, benefiting every product); ran Master Spec §54's exact required sentence through the full pipeline live in a browser and honestly documented the gap between §56's full 11-screen/11-data vision and today's actual deterministic output (Home/Browse only, zero data models) as a disclosed, not-silently-implied limitation (EV-0063, EV-0064, D-0028)

P2-08: Conversational editing, Change Sets, selective regeneration — new ChangeSet model (1:1 with its governing Decision) computing addedCategories by diffing requirements derived from the prior idea vs. the combined (never-discarded) idea text; edit_request intents now generate a Change Set and apply it immediately (non-consequential) or hold it PENDING until Decision approval (consequential); regeneration only happens when addedCategories is non-empty. Also fixed a real regression this work surfaced live in the e2e suite: generateProductIntelligence silently reset a customer's edited unitEconomicsAssumptions on a second call, since ProductState is full-replace — now carries that one customer-editable field forward (EV-0065, EV-0066, D-0029)

P2-09: Version history and restore — getProjectVersionHistory aggregates ProductState/Blueprint/BuildPlan/ChangeSet into one chronological, immutable-by-construction timeline; previewBlueprintRestore computes a real screens/dataModels diff; validateBlueprintRestore re-validates a target version's stored content before restoring; restoreBlueprintVersion creates a new top version with the target's content, never mutating history in between. Restore scoped to Blueprint only (Build Plan is cheaply regenerable; Product State restore has no established use case yet) (EV-0067, EV-0068, D-0030)

P2-12: Migration planning for generated-app data model changes — planDataModelMigration performs the full §28 sequence (schema diff, real data-loss analysis querying actual GeneratedRecord rows per removed field rather than guessing, compatibility notes, ordered migration plan, honest backup requirement disclosing no automated backup mechanism exists, rollback plan referencing P2-09's restore) between any two Blueprint versions; recordMigrationPlanDecision records it as CONSEQUENTIAL when destructive or ROUTINE otherwise, reusing the existing Decision Ledger. Standalone/explicitly-invoked, not wired into applyChangeSet's auto-apply path (EV-0073, EV-0074, D-0033)

P2-13: Export foundation + durable jobs — exportProject() bundles Product State/DNA/Blueprint/Build Plan/GeneratedRecords/generated-app users (allowlisted, never passwordHash)/policy drafts/GovernanceProfile/Truth Status into one structured JSON bundle with honest disclosures (not a deployable package, not a backup); new JobRun model (PENDING/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED, checkpoint, idempotencyKey, attempt) wraps (never modifies) generateApplication via runGenerationJob — idempotent, retryable, real status for the first time. Checkpointing coarse-grained (before/after, not sub-steps) (EV-0075, EV-0076, D-0034)

P2-14: Web and PWA output — syncOutputTargetStatus() tracks output.web/output.pwa/output.ios/output.android independently via the existing Truth Status mechanism (reusing rationale text for §39's richer status vocabulary rather than a new enum), wired automatically into generateApplication; a real per-project Web App Manifest (generateManifest(), derived from actual Project/Product DNA data) served at /org/[orgSlug]/[projectSlug]/manifest.webmanifest and a real minimal (pass-through, no offline caching claimed) service worker at .../sw.js, both wired into the live preview page and verified to genuinely register in a real browser (EV-0077, EV-0078, D-0035)

P2-15: Mobile architecture + generated mobile project — React Native + Expo selected and documented (Master Spec's own suggested example); generateMobileProjectFiles() deterministically produces a real, minimal Expo project scaffold (app.json/package.json/tsconfig.json/App.tsx, a static navigation list reflecting the real Blueprint screen names) from a project's actual data; validateMobileProjectFiles() performs real 'build validation' honestly scoped to JSON parsing + TypeScript/TSX syntax checking via the TS compiler's own parser, genuinely catching malformed code — not a full RN type-check and never a real native build (no Xcode/Android SDK in this environment); generateMobileProject() syncs output.ios/output.android Truth Status to IMPLEMENTED with an honest no-native-build rationale (EV-0079, EV-0080, D-0036)

P2-16: Mobile-commerce classification + Store Readiness Engine — classifyMobileCommerce() deterministically derives §42's transaction category (physical goods/services, digital goods/content/subscriptions, app functionality, donations, marketplaces, regulated products, external account access) from a project's real original idea text via word-boundary keyword matching, honestly reporting unclassified rather than guessing when monetization exists but no category keyword matches; assessStoreReadiness() mirrors the Quality Gate pattern (P2-10) with real checks (mobile project generated/validated, mobile-commerce classification resolved, Terms of Service drafted, Privacy Policy drafted, developer account connected), recording Evidence and syncing a new store.readiness Truth Status subject key to BLOCKED — readinessStatus is a fixed, honest NOT_READY since no Apple/Google developer account integration exists in this build (Phase 3 scope, §61/§65) (EV-0081, EV-0082, D-0037)

P2-17: Studio UI wiring for Phase 2 — closed the repeatedly-disclosed 'no Studio UI surface yet' gap for the highest-value Phase 2 capabilities per Master Spec §6's Simple Mode surfaces: a new Versions section (real chronological history + Blueprint restore, P2-09); Launch section gained real buttons wired to already-tested functions (Run Quality Gate P2-10, Assess store readiness P2-16, Generate mobile project P2-15, per-type legal draft generation P2-11); a new authenticated GET .../export route streams the real P2-13 export bundle as a downloadable file (mirrors the manifest.webmanifest/sw.js route pattern from P2-14); the Trust section now renders every Truth Status entry's real rationale text, making every prior unit's honest detail (Quality Gate failures, Store Readiness blockers, mobile's no-native-build disclosure) visible for the first time without new plumbing. Verified end-to-end through a real browser (e2e/launch-actions.spec.ts), not just at the service layer (EV-0083, D-0038)

P2-EXIT repair cycle (Level 3 review round 1, verdict revise) — fixed both CRITICAL DEFECTs and both DEFECTs the independent reviewer found by live adversarial testing. (1) src/lib/db-versioning.ts's createNextVersion() adds retry-with-jittered-backoff to the read-latest-then-create-next-version race present in all 8 append-only versioned models (Blueprint, BuildPlan, ProductState, ProductDNA, PolicyDocument, TruthStatusEntry, CapabilityRegistryEntry, PlanDefinition) — previously a double-clicked 'Generate app' could crash to a raw Prisma P2002 error instead of succeeding. (2) requireCurrentUserForAction() (src/lib/web/require-user.ts) replaces requireCurrentUser() in all 6 Server Action files — an expired/absent session now redirects to /sign-in instead of crashing. (3) D-0039 explicitly acknowledges, at phase-exit level, that the exact §56 demonstration sentence does not yet produce §56's full stated vision (elevating D-0028's routine self-classification). (4) sw.js now carries the same auth/tenant gate as manifest.webmanifest. Both critical fixes were adversarially self-verified: each was reverted, confirmed to reproduce the reviewer's exact live failure via a new regression test, then restored and reconfirmed passing. Full suite: 382/382 unit+integration (377 prior + 5 new), 12/12 e2e (11 prior + 1 new), clean typecheck/lint/format, production build (EV-0085, D-0040)

P2-EXIT round 2 review and repair (Level 3 review round 2, verdict conditionally accept) — a second independent reviewer re-verified all 4 round-1 fixes live (stress-tested the concurrency fix to 100 concurrent writers, tested the session fix against a different Server Action, re-ran the §56 demonstration test directly, curl'd sw.js/manifest.webmanifest unauthenticated) and confirmed all genuinely fixed, no regression in a fresh audit sample (D-0018, D-0031, D-0033, D-0034). Its own adversarial pass found one new, undisclosed instance of the identical race class: startOrGetJobRun (src/lib/generation/job-runs.ts) could crash with an uncaught P2002 under concurrent calls sharing an idempotencyKey — not customer-reachable today (not wired into any live route), so not a CRITICAL DEFECT, but required disclosure or a fix before the completion report. Fixed immediately rather than only disclosed: startOrGetJobRun now catches the exact conflict and defers to the winner's row (a new resolveExistingJobRun helper), the correct idempotency response — not createNextVersion's retry-a-new-version-number pattern, which does not apply since a JobRun's identity is fixed by its idempotencyKey. Adversarially self-verified the same way: reverted, confirmed a new 10-concurrent-caller regression test reproduces the exact live crash, restored, reconfirmed green. Full suite: 383/383 unit+integration (382 prior + 1 new), 12/12 e2e, clean typecheck/lint/format, production build (EV-0086, D-0041)

P3-01: Real AI provider connection — AnthropicAIProvider (src/lib/ai/anthropic-provider.ts) makes a real Anthropic Messages API call with forced tool-use for a structurally guaranteed ResolvedIntent response; replaces the Phase 1/2 ProviderNotImplementedError placeholder; selected only via AI_PROVIDER=anthropic + a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, mock remains default; registered honestly in the Capability Registry (ai.live_provider_intent_resolution: PROTOTYPE_ONLY — real, tested, never yet exercised against the real API in this environment; ai.live_provider_generation correctly stays SUPPORTED_LATER_PHASE since Blueprint/Build Plan generation itself remains the deterministic template pipeline) (D-0047, EV-0092)

P3-02: Production database/auth hardening + migration and tenant-isolation verification tooling — sign-in brute-force lockout (LoginAttempt table, 5 attempts/15min, checked before password verification, identical behavior for nonexistent emails); Postgres connection pool hardening (bounded pool size, timeouts, onPoolError handler) in src/lib/db.ts; findTenantIsolationViolations (src/lib/tenancy/verify-tenant-isolation.ts) — a real TypeScript-compiler-API static analysis tool computing call-graph reachability to requireProjectAccess/requireOrganizationMembership for every project/organization-scoped function, run against the real codebase (zero unjustified violations, one legitimate disclosed exception classified) and wired into the permanent test suite as a regression gate; findMigrationSafetyViolations (src/lib/db-safety/verify-migration-safety.ts) — scans all applied migrations for destructive SQL, confirms the full 17-migration history is purely additive, also a permanent regression gate (D-0048, EV-0093)

P3-03: Plans, entitlements, usage metering, limits and overages — src/lib/billing/entitlements.ts adds real enforcement on top of Phase 1/2's declared-but-unenforced plan entitlements: getOrganizationUsage (real project-count metering), assertWithinProjectLimit (wired into createProject, real ProjectLimitExceededError), assertExportAllowed (wired into exportProject, real ExportNotAllowedError). Both surfaced gracefully at every real call site (403/redirect, never a raw crash), proven live via e2e (billing-usage.spec.ts; launch-actions.spec.ts updated). Billing page now shows real usage against the limit. Entitlements resolution fails open (unrestricted) when the Plan Registry has no data at all for a plan key (a configuration gap, not a policy to enforce) and falls back to the Free/Explore default when an organization has no subscription row yet. storageMb, teamSeats, deploymentAllowed remain declared, honestly unenforced (no real metering/feature exists yet for any of the three) (D-0049, EV-0094)

P3-04: Production billing -- portal, verified webhooks, reconciliation, failed-payment retries, grace periods, restriction/suspension/restoration/retention/deletion workflows. BillingProvider abstraction (mock + real Stripe, raw crypto/fetch not the SDK) mirroring AIProvider's P3-01 pattern; real Stripe webhook signature verification (HMAC-SHA256, Stripe's documented scheme, tested against self-computed valid/invalid/tampered/stale signatures) at a new /api/webhooks/stripe route; idempotent event processing (new ProcessedWebhookEvent table) mapping 3 real Stripe event types to the pre-existing (Phase 1) deterministic billing state machine; applyBillingLifecycleEventFromWebhook as a deliberate, disclosed no-actor exception (added to the tenant-isolation tool's reviewed list); real billing-portal session creation and drift-detecting (not auto-correcting) reconciliation; billing page UI wiring. Honestly disclosed: never exercised against the real Stripe API (PROTOTYPE_ONLY); no checkout flow exists to link a real customer; only event-driven transitions are wired, the 5 time-based ones need scheduled-job infrastructure this codebase does not have yet. Also fixed a real gap this unit's own validation caught: test/reset-db.ts never cleared the new ProcessedWebhookEvent table, causing 4 false test failures under full-suite (not isolated) runs (D-0050, EV-0095)

P3-05: Customer-owned infrastructure protection + customer-owned integration connections/OAuth. Real, generic OAuth2 authorization-code flow (src/lib/integrations/oauth.ts) on Phase 1's existing IntegrationRequirement/CredentialReference vault -- CSRF-safe single-use state (new OAuthConnectionState table), real token exchange, storage through the existing AES-256-GCM vault, a real live callback Route Handler (/api/integrations/oauth/callback) handling every real failure path gracefully. No concrete third-party provider registered (a product decision, not invented here) -- provider registry genuinely empty, PROTOTYPE_ONLY. Separately: a direct integration test proving Project/IntegrationRequirement/CredentialReference/GeneratedRecord data survives the real, full billing lifecycle unchanged through actual DELETED state (Master Spec S62's guarantee, now tested not just true by inspection) (D-0051, EV-0096)

P3-06: Customer-owned generated-app payment and subscription connections. Real charge-creation mechanism (createGeneratedAppCharge, src/lib/generation/generated-app-payments.ts) charging a generated product's end user through the *customer's own* connected payment-provider account (via P3-05 OAuth) -- distinct from P3-04's Pocket-Studio-own billing. GeneratedAppPaymentProvider abstraction (mock + real Stripe-Connect-shaped implementation using the connected account's own OAuth token, raw fetch not the SDK). Every charge attempt (success or decline) recorded as a real GeneratedAppPayment row. createGeneratedAppCharge and retrieveCredentialSecretForGeneratedApp are the third instance of the deliberate no-actor exception pattern (after authenticateGeneratedAppUser, applyBillingLifecycleEventFromWebhook). Capability Registry corrected: payments.deposits -> PROTOTYPE_ONLY (real mechanism, never wired to the renderer or a live account); payments.subscriptions stays SUPPORTED_LATER_PHASE (no scheduled-job infrastructure to make billing recur). Not yet wired into the generated-app checkout UI (P2-05's renderer) -- disclosed, deferred integration task (D-0052, EV-0097)

P3-02 targeted regression repair (D-0053, EV-0098): a user-directed, repository-backed review against 9 specific security properties of the sign-in rate limiter found 5 real, confirmed defects and repaired all of them without reopening or restarting P3-04/P3-05/P3-06. (1) Composite (email, ipAddress) keying replaces email-only keying, closing a real account-lockout denial-of-service (anyone who knew a victim's email could lock the victim out from anywhere). (2) A cached dummy-hash comparison on the nonexistent-user path closes a real timing side channel (that path previously skipped scrypt entirely, making it measurably faster than the wrong-password path). (3) A Postgres advisory transaction lock keyed by (email, ipAddress) closes a real check-then-act race that let concurrent requests collectively exceed the attempt threshold -- verified live with a 10-concurrent-request test. (4) A new User.lastLoginAt column replaces destructive delete-all-history-on-success behavior, preserving the full LoginAttempt audit trail indefinitely while still correctly bounding future enforcement. (5) The cleanup sweep is now batch-bounded (not an unfiltered platform-wide delete) and no longer auto-triggered on every login (disclosed, awaiting real scheduled-job infrastructure). A genuine implementation bug in the first attempt at fix (3) -- a Prisma transaction rollback silently discarding every recorded failure -- was caught by this same review's own regression tests before being reported complete.

P3-03 verification (this review, no code change): confirmed via git log (commit d045272, real diff matching its stated scope), execution/state.json's durable unitDecomposition record, and live code inspection (src/lib/billing/entitlements.ts exists, wired into createProject/exportProject, 9 passing integration tests) that P3-03 (plans, entitlements, usage metering, limits and overages) was completed under its own correct name, in its correct dependency-ordered position between P3-02 and P3-04 -- not completed under another name, not merged into another unit, not intentionally removed, and not accidentally skipped. No restoration action was needed.

P3-07: Production email. Real EmailProvider abstraction (mock + SmtpEmailProvider, a real SMTP client implementing RFC 5321 directly over node:tls, no library dependency) mirroring the established provider pattern. SMTP chosen over any vendor-specific REST API since it is the one universal, vendor-agnostic email standard (same 'pick the protocol, not the vendor' posture as P3-05's OAuth work) -- works with any real provider via configuration alone. Every send attempt (sent or a real provider decline) durably recorded as a new SentEmail row. Wired to one real transactional trigger: every sign-up now sends a real welcome email (signUpAction), awaited (not fire-and-forget, since Server Action execution contexts can be torn down after redirect()) but never able to block or fail sign-up itself. Honestly disclosed as PROTOTYPE_ONLY -- tested against a fully scripted fake SMTP conversation, never exercised against a real mail server. Also backfilled a real, pre-existing documentation gap: P3-06's GENERATED_APP_PAYMENT_PROVIDER env var was implemented but never added to .env.example (D-0054, EV-0099)

knownLimitations: Blueprint generation (P2-01) is deterministic/template-based, keyed off the Requirements Engine's Impact Analysis categories — not real design intelligence. Every generated Blueprint discloses this via generationMetadata.generatedBy and generationMetadata.method. Real AI-backed generation is Phase 3 scope (§61).

Generation (P2-06) is live at /org/[orgSlug]/[projectSlug]/preview/[screen], but that route is gated by the existing Pocket-Studio-side platform session (requireUserForPage), not a separate unauthenticated end-user-facing route. authenticateGeneratedAppUser verifies real credentials but does not yet establish a session/cookie — GeneratedAppUser/GeneratedRecord still cannot be reached by an actual customer of the generated product, only by the builder previewing it.

Build Plan component trees remain minimal pattern-driven placeholders, not real designed layouts. (Form Input naming was fixed in P2-07 to match a bound data model's real fields, so a genuine field-matched submission now succeeds when a data model is bound — see D-0028.)

The official Phase 2 demonstration (P2-07, Master Spec §56: 'Build a premium booking app for mobile detailers.') runs successfully end to end (GENERATED, VALID, READY, live in a browser) but its honest current output is only the base Home/Browse screens with zero data models — far short of §56's full vision (11 customer screens, 11 owner screens, 11 data types: Services, Packages, Availability, Memberships, etc.). This gap is intentionally NOT closed by hardcoding this one sentence's content, per Master Spec §26's 'not hardcoded preview screens' requirement — closing it honestly requires either a deliberately expanded, reusable domain-template vocabulary or real AI-backed generation (Phase 3, §61). See official-demonstration.integration.test.ts's module comment for the full accounting.

Conversational editing (P2-08) 'selective regeneration' is category-level (regenerate the whole Blueprint/Build Plan, or don't), not screen/field-level — true incremental diffing of individual screens or data models does not exist yet.

Version history (P2-09) aggregates Product State/Blueprint/Build Plan/Change Set into one read-only timeline, and restore exists for Blueprint only — Build Plan and Product State have no restore function yet (Build Plan is cheaply regenerable from a Blueprint; Product State restore has no established use case). The Studio page's Versions section (P2-17) lists this timeline and offers a direct one-click Blueprint restore, but does not surface previewBlueprintRestore's computed screens/dataModels diff first — that remains service-layer only.

The Quality Gate (P2-10) runs 8 real structural/server-side checks but does not run a per-generation browser e2e test or live authorization/tenant fuzzing — tenant isolation is verified structurally (by construction, via P2-04's own tests), not re-tested per Quality Gate invocation. The Studio page's Launch section (P2-17) can now trigger a real run and its pass/fail rationale is visible in Trust, but there is no per-check breakdown view — only the aggregate result and, on failure, the list of failed check names.

FOUNDER-DISCOVERED DEFECT (D-0065/EV-0110, 2026-07-15): the deterministic generation pipeline can produce a structurally VALID Blueprint / READY Build Plan / passing Quality Gate while losing nearly all of an arbitrary customer description's explicit product meaning. Root-caused and live-reproduced against a real, detailed HomeBase household-management description: analyzeImpact() (impact-analysis.ts)'s fixed 15-category/~90-keyword substring classifier matched only 2 of 15 categories; the resulting Blueprint had roles:['customer'] only (no Parent/Child), one generic 'Record' data model (no chores/groceries/expenses/appointments/rewards), and workflows:[] despite an explicit recurring-task workflow being described. validateBlueprint() and runQualityGate() are both intentionally structural-only (by their own docstrings) with no semantic-coverage dimension, so both passed cleanly on the hollow output. The Studio page also renders businessModelBrief.revenueModel ('No revenue model was described') directly above monetizationRecommendations ('one-time payment') with no fact-vs-recommendation label, reproducing a founder-observed contradiction. This is not a HomeBase-specific bug -- it reproduces for any product description that does not happen to use this pipeline's fixed keyword set. A domain-agnostic semantic-compilation repair (canonical semantic product model, AI-backed semantic understanding with honest deterministic fallback, semantic coverage engine, Quality Gate/Truth Status extensions, multi-domain regression corpus with a novel holdout) is authorized and in progress -- see the forthcoming pre-implementation report in execution/architecture/. Blocks: any claim that Pocket Studio deeply understands or preserves an arbitrary customer's product description; does not block the previously-established Founder Alpha verdict for the capabilities that verdict already covered, but materially limits how much semantic trust to place in any Blueprint/Build Plan/Truth Status produced by the deterministic (mock) provider for a product outside this pipeline's narrow keyword coverage.
